qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Spec-driven OEM qualification barriers in automotive and aerospace coatings create customer switching costs, but heavy B2B buyer power and cyclical raw-material input costs cap pricing power and keep returns on capital sub-hurdle.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC < 12%, REJECT). Spec-driven industrial, automotive OEM, and aerospace coatings face powerful procurement counterparties and volatile raw material input cycles, resulting in a 10-year median ROIC of ~11.2% (ranging 8.2%-11.2% across 2020-2025), structurally below the 12% quality hurdle.
qualitative.evidence: 10-year median ROIC of 11.2% (2020: 10.4%, 2021: 9.1%, 2022: 8.25%, 2023: 11.1%, 2024: 11.2%, 2025: ~10.3-11.7%). Operating margins track in the 11.5%-13.5% range, trailing controlled-distribution peers like Sherwin-Williams (14%-16%+ ROIC, 16%+ EBIT margins). Recent divestiture of US/Canada architectural coatings ($550M sale to AIP in late 2024) prunes low-margin retail volume but leaves a capital-intensive B2B industrial core.
